items.question: Which engine powers the AS350 B3e?
items.explanation: B3e is equipped with a Turbomeca Arriel 2D engine.

items.question: What is the Arriel 2D maximum takeoff power rating (MTOP)?
items.explanation: MTOP (uninstalled, ISA, sea level) is 641 kW (860 SHP).

items.question: What is the Arriel 2D maximum continuous power rating (MCP)?
items.explanation: MCP is 551 kW (739 SHP).

items.question: What is the main rotor diameter on the AS350 B3e?
items.explanation: The main rotor diameter is 10.69 m (35.07 ft).

items.question: What is the nominal main rotor speed?
items.explanation: Nominal NR is 386 rpm.

items.question: What is the nominal tail rotor speed?
items.explanation: Nominal tail rotor speed is 2044 rpm.

items.question: What is the total fuel capacity?
items.explanation: Total fuel capacity is 540 l (427 kg).

items.question: What is the usable fuel in the standard tank?
items.explanation: Usable fuel (standard tank) is 538.7 l (425.6 kg).

items.question: What is the usable fuel in the crash resistant tank?
items.explanation: Usable fuel (crash resistant tank) is 538 l (425 kg).

items.question: On the Caution and Warning Panel, what do red and amber lights indicate?
options: Red: immediate action; Amber: action can be delayed
Red: maintenance only; Amber: immediate action
Red: audio only; Amber: visual only
items.explanation: Red warning lights require immediate action; amber caution lights allow action to be delayed.

items.question: How are audio warnings activated?
options: Set [HORN] to ON on the central console
Set [INV] to ON on the overhead panel
Set [GENE] to OFF on the console
Set [BATT] to ON on the console
items.explanation: Audio alarms are generated through the ICS and are activated when [HORN] is set to ON.

items.question: What supplies the Caution and Warning Panel (CWP)?
options: Dual 28 VDC power supply protected by circuit breakers
items.explanation: The CWP is supplied by a dual 28 VDC power supply and protected by circuit breakers.

items.question: Where are WACS and FDR fault indicators installed (post MOD 07-20112 or MOD 07-20228)?
items.explanation: WACS and FDR fault indicators are installed on the overhead panel.

items.question: Which audio tone corresponds to an MTOP overlimit?
items.explanation: ASU No.1 manages audio warnings: Gong for red alarms; continuous low tone for MTOP overlimit.

items.question: How is the VEMD architected?
options: Two processing modules (LANE 1 & LANE 2) and one display module
One processing module and two display modules
Three display modules and a single processing unit
Two FADEC channels and one display module
items.explanation: The VEMD comprises LANE 1, LANE 2 processing modules and a display module with two screens.

items.question: Which operating modes are available on the VEMD?
items.explanation: Three modes: OPERATIONAL (engine/vehicle/FLI/flight report/engine power check), CONFIGURATION, and MAINTENANCE.

items.question: Where is the hydraulic cut-off switch located?
items.explanation: The hydraulic cut-off switch is a guarded switch mounted on the collective grip.

items.question: Which sources supply the DC electrical network?
options: Starter-generator, 15 Ah battery (optional second), 28 V EPU
Two alternators and a 12 V battery
items.explanation: The DC network is supplied by a starter-generator, a 15 Ah battery (optional second) and a 28 V external power unit.

items.question: What does the PITOT amber caution indicate?
options: Pitot heating not operating, switch OFF or system failure
Static ports blocked by ice only
items.explanation: An amber PITOT caution indicates the heating system is not operating, the [PITOT] switch is OFF, or the system has failed.

items.question: Post MOD 07-20039, what is the hydraulic system regulating pressure?
items.explanation: The regulator is set to 60 bar (870 psi) post MOD 07-20039 (40 bar pre-mod).

items.question: On the B3e instrument panel, what does the rotor speed indicator display alongside NR?
items.explanation: The B3e's Arriel 2D terminology uses N2 for the power turbine speed indicator, shown alongside NR — unlike the B3 2B1, which labels this indicator NR/Nf.

items.question: Post MOD 07-20112/07-20228, what fault indicators are added to the overhead panel?
items.explanation: A lighting plate on the overhead panel adds WACS (Wireless Airborne Communication System) and FDR (Flight Data Recorder) fault indicators.

items.question: Where is the guarded EBCAU (engine back-up control) test switch located on the B3e?
items.explanation: On the B3e, the guarded EBCAU test switch is located on the overhead panel.

items.question: What is the purpose of the B3e's Pulse Light function?
options: It flashes the taxi and landing lights alternately to improve aircraft detectability and reduce bird strikes
It dims the cockpit lighting automatically at night
It tests the CWP warning lights on startup
It flashes the anti-collision light faster in icing conditions
items.explanation: Pulse Light blinks and flashes the taxi and landing headlights alternately, improving detectability in heavy traffic and reducing the likelihood of bird strikes. It is automatically deactivated if the landing or taxi light is switched on.

items.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the B3e's optional NVG-compatible cockpit features?
items.explanation: The anti-collision light is explicitly NOT NVG compatible; using the landing light can help limit disturbance to the pilot instead.

items.question: What power class is the Turbomeca Arriel 2D engine fitted to the B3e?
items.explanation: The Arriel 2D is a 700 kW (937 SHP) class turboshaft engine, higher than the 2B1's 650 kW (870 hp) class.

items.question: What additional cockpit indication appears on the B3e (post MOD 07-20039) when operating close to servo transparency?
options: A LIMIT light on the CWP with a 285 Hz continuous tone
An automatic reduction of collective travel
items.explanation: Post MOD 07-20039, operating close to servo transparency triggers a LIMIT light on the CWP plus a 285 Hz continuous tone, based on weight, altitude, OAT, airspeed and load factor.

items.question: On the B3e, where may the static pressure ports be located, in addition to under the cabin?
options: On top of the main rotor mast
items.explanation: The two static pressure ports are located under the cabin, or in the tail boom if that configuration is installed.

items.question: On an AIRS-400 cockpit camera, what does a steady red LED indicate?
options: GPS antenna not plugged in / not functioning, or a critical error
items.explanation: On the AIRS-400 camera, steady red means the GPS antenna is not plugged in or not functioning, or a critical error has occurred (flashing red is also a critical error).

items.question: The B3e cockpit video camera installation can be fitted with which two camera systems?
items.explanation: The B3e's cockpit video camera section documents two possible systems: the Vision 1000 camera and the AIRS-400 camera, each with its own LED status code table.

items.question: After the hydraulic pressure cut-off test on the B3e, what is the normal accumulator re-pressurization time?
items.explanation: On the B3e, normal accumulator re-pressurization takes 3 to 4 seconds; a time reduced to 1 second or increased beyond 4 seconds indicates a faulty accumulator.

items.question: What type of main rotor hub does the B3e use, and what is distinctive about it?
options: STARFLEX hub, with no ball bearings and no lubrication system
A fully articulated hub with elastomeric bearings requiring regular lubrication
A teetering hub identical to the tail rotor
A rigid hub with hydraulic dampers
items.explanation: The semi-rigid "STARFLEX" main rotor hub has no ball bearings nor a lubrication system; flapping is achieved through the composite star arms, with lead-lag and pitch hinges via elastomeric components.

items.question: On the B3e, how many main rotor servos does the hydraulic system power, and how are they arranged?
options: Three: one longitudinal and two lateral
Two: one longitudinal and one lateral
Four: two longitudinal and two lateral
One combined servo for all axes
items.explanation: There are three main rotor servos (one longitudinal, two lateral) plus a separate tail rotor servo for yaw control.

items.question: On the B3e, what distinguishes SAMM main rotor servos from Dunlop servos?
options: SAMM servos have an input play locking system; Dunlop servos do not
Dunlop servos are electrically actuated; SAMM servos are not
SAMM servos only work on the tail rotor
There is no functional difference between them
items.explanation: SAMM servos include an input play locking system to reduce control freeplay in non-assisted (bypass) mode, which can cause a brief cyclic movement during pressurization; Dunlop lateral servos do not have this device.

items.question: On the B3e, where are the cockpit breaker panels located?
options: Left (44α) and right (30/31/32α, 16α) sides of the cockpit console, plus a 50α panel in the RH cargo compartment
All breakers are in a single overhead panel
Only in the RH cargo compartment
items.explanation: The B3e's cockpit breaker panels sit on the left (44α) and right (30/31/32α, 16α) sides of the console, with an additional 50α breaker panel in the RH cargo compartment.

items.question: How many separate circuits provide cabin ventilation on the B3e?
options: Two: front ventilation and overhead ventilation
items.explanation: Two separate circuits ventilate the cabin: front ventilation (via two ducts to the crew) and overhead ventilation (via a ram air scoop through the structure posts).

items.question: How is cabin heating and demisting air produced on the B3e?
options: By mixing hot P2 air bled from the engine with outside air drawn from under the cabin floor
By an electric resistive heater in the cabin floor
By diverting exhaust gas directly into the cabin
items.explanation: Heating and demisting are achieved by mixing hot P2 air bled from the engine with outside air drawn from under the cabin floor, channelled to heating and demisting outlets.
